title: Where does AI actually help in stock research, and where does it quietly make numbers up?
author: West-Structure-4030
selftext:
Plenty of posts here are about AI bots trading, fewer about using AI for the research step before a trade.

Where it seems genuinely useful: summarizing a long 10-K or earnings call into what changed vs last year, turning a vague idea like "cheap semis with improving margins" into actual screening criteria, and steelmanning the bear case on something you already like.

Where it goes wrong: asking it for financial figures from memory (revenue, margins and share counts come back confidently wrong or stale), peer comparisons with companies that don't really compete, and valuation math where one bad input carries through everything.

The fix seems to be feeding it the actual numbers from filings or a data source you trust and letting it reason over them, instead of letting it recall them. Any figure it gives without a source, treat as unverified.

Disclosure: I'm building a US stock research tool with an AI research workflow, so I think about this a lot.

How are you using it? Do you let AI pull the data, or only reason over data you give it?

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body: Only over data I give it. Even then I ask it to quote the exact line it's using, because sometimes it "cleans up" a number from the filing into a slightly different one and the reasoning still sounds totally fine.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: only over data I give it, same as Aoideus. the place it fails me most is peers. it'll call two companies competitors because they share a sector code, and the comparison reads fine until you check what they actually sell.

comments.author: a_hooulookinat
comments.body: Summarizing filings and challenging an investment thesis seem like genuinely useful applications. I'd never trust an AI generated revenue figure without checking the original filing though. I follow market movements through moon but when I'm interested in the company behind a stock, accurate financial data matters more than a beautifully written explanation built on questionable numbers.

comments.author: AstraEyeLabs
comments.body: Reason over data you feed it, never recall. The tell is a figure with no window or source attached, so I check those two before anything else. What are you using to pull the numbers in, filings directly or a data feed?
